correctness.rationale: Every value is derived from the exact characteristic function for a binary majority of correct versus incorrect predictors, with uniform tie and empty-coalition zero. For \(a,b\ge1\) the global sum of correct-singleton and all-incorrect inequalities forces \(\varepsilon\ge (a-v(N))/(a+1)\); when \(a\ge b+2\), averaging all coalitions with b+1 correct plus all b incorrect yields \(\varepsilon\ge(a-b-1)/(a-b)\). Their crossover is exactly \(a=2b+1\). Explicit efficient type-symmetric credits attain the maximum of these bounds; winning, losing and tied coalitions are individually bounded, with the only low-epsilon tie exceptions \((1,1)\) and \((2,1)\) directly checked. Homogeneous types follow by singleton sum and zero allocation. Exact-rational checker verifies 1088 profiles/312544 constraints and 54 independent full unsymmetrized LPs. The algebraic proof, not finite tests, handles arbitrary counts.

value.rationale: Minimizing worst coalition shortfall is a natural quantitative stability complement to marginal attribution in the published voting-ensemble cooperative game. The theorem is a complete infinite-family exact natural invariant with explicit sharp coalition certificates and a switch in the identity of the obstructing coalition at \(a=2b+1\). It avoids arbitrary numeric slices and informs feasible stability slack for a single test example; the dataset-averaged and constrained-payoff problems are explicitly not claimed.
